rev = {'May':412380,'Jun':431205,'Jul':389640}
costs_items = {'May':151120,'Jun':158540,'Jul':158280}   # line-item sums
costs_stated= {'May':151120,'Jun':158240,'Jul':158280}   # as stated
new={'May':86,'Jun':74,'Jul':63}; churn={'May':17,'Jun':22,'Jul':31}
op={'May':342,'Jun':361,'Jul':298}; cl={'May':315,'Jun':350,'Jul':291}

R=sum(rev.values())
for label,C in (('line-items',sum(costs_items.values())),('stated',sum(costs_stated.values()))):
    net=R-C
    print(f"{label}: costs={C:,} net={net:,} margin={net/R*100:.1f}%  (raw {net/R*100:.4f})")

print("Revenue total:", f"{R:,}")
adds = sum(new.values())-sum(churn.values())
print("new",sum(new.values()),"churn",sum(churn.values()),"adds",adds)
O,L=sum(op.values()),sum(cl.values())
print(f"opened={O} closed={L} rate={L/O*100:.1f}% (raw {L/O*100:.4f})")
for m in ('Jun','Jul'):
    p={'Jun':'May','Jul':'Jun'}[m]
    g=(rev[m]-rev[p])/rev[p]*100
    print(f"{m} growth {g:.1f}% (raw {g:.4f}) delta={rev[m]-rev[p]:+,}")
# monthly detail
for m in rev:
    n=rev[m]-costs_items[m]
    print(f"{m}: rev={rev[m]:,} cost={costs_items[m]:,} net={n:,} margin={n/rev[m]*100:.1f}% adds={new[m]-churn[m]:+d} close={cl[m]/op[m]*100:.1f}%")
EOF

input.command:
cat > Q-REPORT.md << 'EOF'
# Quarterly operations report — Q2/Q3 2026 (May–July)

## Summary

The quarter delivered €1,233,225 of revenue against €467,940 of costs, for a net
of €765,285 and a margin of 62.1%. Headline profitability remains strong, but the
shape of the quarter matters more than the total: performance peaked in June and
deteriorated sharply in July.

Revenue rose 4.6% in June to €431,205, then fell 9.6% in July to €389,640 — below
where the quarter started in May. Costs, meanwhile, held essentially flat between
June and July (€158,540 and €158,280), so the entire revenue shortfall dropped
straight through to the bottom line. Monthly margin ran 63.4%, 63.2% and 59.4%
across May, June and July; the July compression is a cost base sized for a revenue
level we did not hit, not a cost overrun.

The customer picture points the same direction and arguably leads it. We added 153
net customers over the quarter, but the monthly trend decayed steadily: +69, +52,
+32. Both sides of that number moved against us — new signings fell each month
(86, 74, 63) while churn rose each month (17, 22, 31), nearly doubling from May to
July. Support was the quarter's bright spot, closing 956 of 1,001 tickets for a
95.5% close rate, improving month over month to 97.7% in July.

Read together, the quarter is best characterised as one good month and one clearly
weak one, with a consistent downward trend in customer momentum running underneath
the whole period. The July revenue drop should be treated as a signal to
investigate rather than a single bad month.

## Key figures

| Figure | Value |
|---|---|
| Quarterly revenue | €1,233,225 |
| Quarterly costs | €467,940 |
| Net | €765,285 |
| Margin | 62.1% |
| Net customer adds | 153 |
| Ticket close rate | 95.5% |
| June revenue growth | 4.6% |
| July revenue growth | -9.6% |

## Notes

- **Churn is the trend to watch.** Churn climbed every month (17 → 22 → 31) while
  new signings fell every month (86 → 74 → 63). Net adds more than halved from May
  to July. This is a two-sided deterioration, not a one-off cohort expiring.

- **July's margin drop is structural, not a cost event.** Costs were flat June to
  July (−€260) while revenue fell €41,565. No cost line ran away; the margin fell
  because revenue did.

- **Cloud spend rises every month regardless of revenue** (€21,310 → €23,940 →
  €24,760, +16.2% over the quarter). In July it grew while revenue fell 9.6%. Worth
  confirming this tracks usage rather than drift.

- **Marketing was cut 20.7% in July** (€21,400 → €16,980) in the same month
  signings hit their quarterly low. The reports do not establish a causal link, but
  the two should be looked at together before setting Q4 budget.

- **Support volume fell with the customer trend.** Tickets opened dropped from 361
  in June to 298 in July (−17.5%). Close rate improved to 97.7%, though some of the
  gain likely reflects lighter load rather than throughput alone.

- **Data discrepancy in the June monthly.** June's stated total cost (€158,240) does
  not match the sum of its own cost lines (€158,540) — a €300 gap. This report uses
  the line-item sum as authoritative. The difference is immaterial to every figure
  above (margin is 62.1% either way), but the June monthly should be corrected at
  source.
EOF
echo "written:"; wc -l Q-REPORT.md; git status --short

content.text:
`Q-REPORT.md` is written — three second-level headings in the required order, all eight row labels present, no commits made.

**Headline figures:** €1,233,225 revenue, €467,940 costs, €765,285 net, 62.1% margin, 153 net adds, 95.5% close rate, June +4.6%, July −9.6%.

Two things worth your attention:

**A data discrepancy in the June monthly.** Its stated total cost (€158,240) doesn't match the sum of its own cost lines (€158,540) — a €300 gap. May and July both reconcile exactly. I used the line-item sum as authoritative, since the total is the derived figure; the choice is immaterial to every reported number (margin rounds to 62.1% either way). Flagged in Notes for correction at source.

**The quarter's totals hide its trend.** The 62.1% margin is healthy, but the monthly path is 63.4% → 63.2% → 59.4%, and July revenue closed below where May started. The clearest signal is customer momentum: net adds ran +69, +52, +32, with signings falling and churn nearly doubling (17 → 22 → 31) every month. I wrote the Summary to lead with the quarter's shape rather than its totals, since a leadership reader who takes only the headline away would miss this.

Notes also flags cloud spend rising every month independent of revenue (+16.2%), and a 20.7% marketing cut landing in the same month signings hit their low — the monthlies don't establish a causal link there, so I've presented it as something to examine together before Q4 budget rather than as a finding.
